en.title: Google OA #40: Longest All-Zero Subarray
en.description:
Given a non-negative integer array A of length n, and integers X and Y. Two operations are available:
Operation 1: choose any index i (0≤i<n) and set A[i]=A[i]−1;
Operation 2: choose any index i and set A[i]=0.
Operation 1 can be used at most X times, and operation 2 at most Y times. Find the maximum length of a contiguous subarray consisting entirely of 0s after the operations.
en.input: The first line contains three integers n, X, Y; the second line contains n integers A[0..n−1]. 1≤n≤100000, 0≤A[i]≤10^9, 0≤X≤10^15, 0≤Y≤n.
en.output: Output one integer, the maximum length of an all-0 contiguous subarray (possibly 0).
en.explanation:
Example 1: A=[4,3,0,1], X=2, Y=1. Apply operation 2 to index 1 to get [4,0,0,1], then apply operation 1 once to index 3 to get [4,0,0,0]; the all-0 subarray has length 3.
Example 2: only operation 1 can be used; [1,0,3] needs 4 uses and [2,1,0] needs 3, so the answer is 3.
Example 3: two uses of operation 2 set indices 0 and 1 to 0, giving [0,0,0,5], so the answer is 3.
hints: Each positive number in the window costs either one use of operation 2 or as many uses of operation 1 as its value.
Operation 2 should be saved for the largest numbers in the window.
The cost never decreases as the window grows, so you can use two pointers together with two ordered sets.
